headline.title: As AI agents become employees, NewCore emerges with $66M to give them identities
headline.summary: NewCore has raised $66 million to develop solutions aimed at managing AI agents as they increasingly take on roles within organizations. The company emphasizes that the future of enterprise security will focus on the identities and management of these AI agents rather than traditional human employees.

articles.title: A satellite just learned to find things on its own — here’s what that means
articles.summary: In April, an Earth observation satellite successfully autonomously identified specific targets for the first time. This advancement signifies a major step forward in satellite technology and autonomous search capabilities.

articles.title: Meta Tapped a Pentagon Supplier to Prototype Face Recognition for Its Glasses
articles.summary: Meta has partnered with Rank One, a Pentagon supplier, to develop face recognition technology for its smart glasses application. Rank One's board includes notable figures from the CIA and FBI, indicating a strong background in security and technology.

articles.title: The AI layoff wave is becoming a powder keg
articles.summary: As tens of thousands of workers face layoffs in the AI sector, a select group of industry insiders is amassing significant wealth, highlighting a stark disparity in the economic impact of AI advancements. This growing divide raises concerns about the sustainability and ethical implications of the current AI-driven job market.

articles.title: Orchestra-o1: Omnimodal Agent Orchestration
articles.summary: The article introduces "Orchestra-o1," a new framework for orchestrating multi-agent systems that addresses the limitations of existing orchestration methods by enabling interaction across heterogeneous modalities. This advancement aims to enhance task decomposition and collaboration among agents in complex environments.

articles.title: AFFORDANCE20Q: Evaluating Affordance Reasoning from Physical Properties
articles.summary: The article introduces AFFORDANCE20Q, a new benchmark designed to evaluate affordance reasoning in Large Language Models (LLMs) by focusing on the inference of action possibilities from an object's physical properties without relying on explicit object identities. This approach aims to enhance the models' ability to reason over physical characteristics rather than depend on memorized mappings.

articles.title: Can Editing 1 Neuron Fix Repetition Loops in LLMs?
articles.summary: Research on Gemma 4 instruction-tuned models reveals that they frequently fall into repetition loops when tasked with long factual enumeration prompts, with failure rates reaching up to 95%. The study suggests that editing a single neuron may not effectively resolve these persistent issues.

articles.title: GMN4AD: Graph Matching Network for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis with Test-Time Domain Adaptation using Multi-centered Structure Magnetic Resonance Imaging
articles.summary: Researchers have developed GMN4AD, a Graph Matching Network designed to enhance Alzheimer's Disease diagnosis through test-time domain adaptation using multi-centered structural Magnetic Resonance Imaging (sMRI). This approach aims to improve early detection, particularly during the mild cognitive impairment stage, which is crucial for timely intervention.

articles.title: Pix2Pix-Hybrid: Structure-Guided Conditional Synthesis of Hajj Crowd Images with Multi-Channel Conditioning and Weak Attribute Supervision
articles.summary: The paper introduces Pix2Pix-Hybrid (P2P-H), a hybrid conditional GAN designed for synthesizing Hajj crowd images to aid in crowd-counting model development, addressing the scarcity of annotated images and privacy concerns during large gatherings. P2P-H utilizes a U-Net generator for structure-guided synthesis and incorporates multi-channel conditioning and weak attribute supervision to enhance data augmentation.

articles.title: No Accidental Software Agent First Canonical Code for Human Code Entropy Reduction and 30 to 500 times Lower Frontier Model Requirements
articles.summary: A recent paper on arXiv discusses the challenges faced by frontier coding models in learning from human code repositories, which often contain accidental entropy alongside valuable signals. The authors propose a canonical code approach aimed at reducing this entropy, potentially lowering model requirements by 30 to 500 times.

articles.title: Hy-Embodied-0.5-VLA: From Vision-Language-Action Models to a Real-World Robot Learning Stack
articles.summary: The article introduces Hy-Embodied-0.5-VLA (HyVLA-0.5), an integrated system designed for robot learning that encompasses data collection, model design, pre-training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning post-training, and real-world deployment. Each component of the system is outlined to highlight its specific function within the overall learning stack.

articles.title: Moonlight in Latent Space: Chirality and Structural Correspondence Between Beethoven's Op. 27 No. 2 and Machine Learning Mechanisms
articles.summary: The article presents a computational analysis demonstrating that the three movements of Beethoven's "Moonlight Sonata" correspond structurally to three distinct machine learning architectures. The study employs various analytical techniques to reveal insights about the relationship between musical composition and machine learning mechanisms.
